rows.grounds: compound of darī (cleft, cave) and rūpa (form); describes a shape of harīkā
past passive participle of root khyā (to proclaim, know)
compound of sarva (all), doṣa (defect), bhaya (fear), and āvaha (bringing)

items.question: How is the cleft-shaped harīkā classified and what danger does it bring?
premises: The cleft-shaped form is recognized as a type of harīkā.
This cleft-shaped form is classified as threefold.
This form brings fear arising from all defects.
items.inference: Therefore, the cleft-shaped harīkā constitutes a threefold category associated with the danger of all defects.
uncertainties: The precise ritual or material referent of harīkā in this context is not specified in the verse.
items.plain_english: The cleft-shaped form is known to be threefold and brings the fear of all defects.
